sections.title: Traction: 72 V pack, controller, motor, DC-DC
12 V power: battery, fuses, key, dash rail, bucks
Shinegle low voltage: key, F-N-R, throttle, sensors, programmer
Drive: 4WD, diff lock, tray, power steering
Control box inside: Pico 2 and its boards
12 V signals into the control box (opto board)
CAN buses: main Teryx bus and the steering bus
RC box: steering by remote (fake torque sensor)
Dash computer: Pi 5, screen, cameras, USB, audio

PACK.name: Traction battery pack
PACK.note: 72 V. Size TBC (the range maths assumes 7.5 kWh)
PACK.check: Battery pack make, size (kWh), and where its main fuse is. Photo the label

HV_ISO.name: 150 A air-break switch
HV_ISO.note: SG12X2 manual Fig. 2 puts B+ through it
HV_ISO.check: Is the air-break switch fitted, and where? Photo it

CONTACTOR.name: Main contactor
CONTACTOR.note: SG1810 fault 13 is "main contactor or brake fault", so there is probably one. Coil wiring not in any manual we have
CONTACTOR.check: Is there a main contactor between the pack and the controller? Photo it and trace its two small coil wires

SG1202.name: Shinegle SG1202 controller
SG1202.note: Full J1 pinout in config/shinegle-sg1202.yaml and docs/img/sg1202-wiring.svg

CAN_H.desc: CAN H (optional on this model, pins TBC)

DCDC.name: DC-DC converter 72 V to 12 V
DCDC.note: Charges the 12 V battery. Rating TBC; it decides how long winch + steering can run
DCDC.check: DC-DC label (amps out), where its 72 V feed comes from, and whether it is isolated (does its 12 V negative join the pack negative?)

KIT_KEY.name: Shinegle kit key switch
KIT_KEY.note: The kit comes with its own key switch. Is it the Teryx key, or a second one?
KIT_KEY.check: Is the kit key the same switch as the Teryx key? Meter what voltage reaches J1-1 with the key on (12 V or 72 V)

ESTOP.name: E-stop button
ESTOP.note: For RC mode. In series with KSI so it cuts drive with no software

FNR.name: F-N-R switch
FNR.note: Physical switch straight to the controller. The reverse side is also tapped for the control box

PROG.name: SG1810 handheld programmer
PROG.note: Only plugged in for setup. Carries 12 V, never into USB

BAT12.name: 12 V aux battery
BAT12.note: Kept after the conversion. Charged by the DC-DC

GND_STAR.name: Ground point (star)
GND_STAR.note: One solid chassis ground near the fuse block. Every 12 V ground goes here

FB.name: Blade fuse block
FB.note: 12 fuses in use. Small loads that can go out together share a fuse (front bars in pairs, trailer tail + stop, interior bar + accessory). All four front bars are NOT on one fuse, so one fault can't black out the front at night. The winch, control box power, key, power hold and each actuator keep their own. Sam's 12-way (in the post) is used, so it is full with no spares; add a small 6-way next to it if more circuits come
FB.check: Check the 12-way's rating (want 30 A per way, about 100 A total, a cover). Read the front bar labels. Each pair (1+4, 2+3) must draw under about 12 A together (about 140 W) to share a 15 A fuse. If not, give each bar its own 10 A again

F3.desc: rear floods (MOSFET 7-8) + relay 1 trailer reverse pin

F6.desc: winch hand switches, tray limits, trailer reed

F7.desc: extras - interior bar + relay 7 accessory (phone charger, trailer cam)

FB2.name: Small 6-way blade fuse block (stock lights + beacon)
FB2.note: Next to the 12-way, which is full. Fed off the 12-way's feed stud through its own 30 A fuse. All 6 ways used (way 6 feeds the stock brake switch so the brake lights are on a known fuse, always live)

F5.desc: backup lights toggle (low beams + tails + trailer tail)

F6.desc: brake light switch feed (brake lights + trailer stop backup)

RAIL.name: Dash 12 V rail
RAIL.note: Key OR relay 8 (power hold). Stays up after key-off until the Pico lets go

TVS.name: 1.5KE18A TVS diode
TVS.note: Clamps spikes on the dash rail

PI_BUCK.name: Potted 5 V 10 A buck (12/24 V in)
PI_BUCK.note: Sealed car-type 12/24 V to 5 V 10 A (50 W) buck, input 8-35 V or wider. Feeds the Pi 5 (about 16 W with the AI HAT+ 2) and the 4G board (2 A peaks), so about 30 W worst case of its 50 W. Wide input rides out spikes the Mini560 (20 V max) couldn't
PI_BUCK.check: Measure its output on the bench under load: 5.0-5.25 V. The Pi flags low voltage below about 4.6 V

SCREEN_PSU.name: Screen 12 V supply
SCREEN_PSU.note: LTC3780 buck-boost board (5-32 V in, set to 12.0 V, 80 W) in the Pi box. Keeps the screen on a steady 12 V while the battery swings 11-14.4 V. No reverse-polarity protection, so it sits after the fuse. Skip it if the screen's own board says 9-36 V in
SCREEN_PSU.check: Read the label on the screen's power brick (volts and amps)

PICO.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2
PICO.note: Talks to the Pi over CAN only. No USB lead to the Pi; reflash with a laptop on its own USB port in the workshop

DEBUG.name: Debug UART header
DEBUG.note: Inside the box. Vehicle lock workshop reset

PICO_CAN.name: MCP2515 CAN module (control box)
PICO_CAN.note: Blue AliExpress MCP2515 board (8 MHz crystal) with its 5 V TJA1050 swapped for a 3.3 V SN65HVD230 (same pins), so the whole board runs on 3.3 V. Never fit one with the TJA1050 still on: it puts 5 V on the Pico pins

EPS_CAN.name: MCP2515 CAN module (steering bus)
EPS_CAN.note: Own 500 kbit/s bus to the steering ECU. INT not wired, the Pico polls it for the ECU's replies

MCP2.name: Second MCP23017 (0x21)
MCP2.note: Steering enable and drive lock relays, and the trailer input on B0. Newer MCP23017 chips say GPA7/GPB7 are outputs only (Microchip datasheet rev D on), so the trailer input moved here off MCP1 B7

PCA.name: PCA9685 16-ch PWM board (0x40)
PCA.note: Every light that isn't a front bar or the cabin bar dims through this (docs/lights.md). Wires soldered straight to the pads, no header pins. VCC 3.3 V so the outputs are 3.3 V, which the MOSFET boards (3-20 V input) and the BTS7960s (3.3 V logic like BTS1-3) take. Leave V+ (servo power) empty. OE tied low on the board. PWM0 trailer bar, 1-10 stock lights on BTS7960 4-8, 11-12 rear floods, 13-14 beacon amber / white on BTS7960 9, 15 BTS7960 enable. All outputs are off at power-up

ADS1.name: ADS1115 ADC (0x48)
ADS1.note: ALERT pin left free so GP22 can be the steering CAN chip select (read "ready" over I2C)

OPTO.name: 8-ch opto board (PC817, 12 V in)
OPTO.note: All 8 channels used. OUT8 (trailer) goes to MCP2 B0. A second 8-ch board (AliExpress cart) gives spare inputs on MCP2 B1-B6 (B7 is output only)

RELAYS.name: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8
RELAYS.note: One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V
RELAYS.check: Does the relay board click from 3.3 V logic? Active high or low? Relays are SRD-05VDC type, 10 A at 28-30 V DC. Keep each load under about 7 A. Nothing on the relays gets near that now the floods are on the MOSFET board (relay 1 only feeds the trailer reversing lamp)

RELAYS2.name: 16-ch relay board, channels 9-16 (2 used, 6 spare)
RELAYS2.note: Same board as RELAYS. Relay 9 steering enable, relay 10 drive lock (uses the NC contact)
RELAYS2.check: Relay 10 is rated 30 V DC. If the Shinegle KSI turns out to be 72 V (see KIT_KEY), swap relay 10 for one rated 80 V DC or more

BTS4.name: BTS7960 4 (left headlight low / high)
BTS4.note: Used as two high-side switches, not a motor bridge. VCC from the Pico 3.3 V like BTS1-3. EN (R_EN + L_EN) from PCA9685 PWM15 with a 10k to ground, so the lamps stay off until the Pico is running

BTS9.name: BTS7960 9 (roof beacon amber / white)
BTS9.note: Two-colour beacons usually share one earth wire, so the colours are switched on the + side like the stock lamps: RPWM amber, LPWM white

MOSFET.name: 8-ch isolated MOSFET board (low side, all 8 used)
MOSFET.note: Sam's board: 8-channel opto-isolated MOSFET driver, DC 3.7-27 V, 10 A per channel, PWM input 3-20 V, 0-20 kHz. 1-4 front bars, 5 cabin bar, 6 trailer bar, 7-8 rear floods. Low side switching, so each light's + comes from its fuse and its - goes to an OUT pin
MOSFET.check: The listing must say 3.3 V input, PNP / high-level trigger (firmware drives the pins high for on; pins sit low at boot so lights stay off), at least 24 V load and 10 A per channel. If it only says 5 A, use single LR7843 modules instead. Low side switching only works if each light's - wire isn't joined to its metal body. Meter a bar's - lead to its housing (and the floods and trailer bar), it must read open. If one reads shorted, that light needs a high side switch

LB_TRL.name: Trailer light bar (Sam's spare)
LB_TRL.note: On the trailer, through the 8-pin plug. On/off from the dash and the phone remote; only live when the trailer plug is in

FLOOD_L.name: Rear flood left (4 in pod)
FLOOD_L.note: Outside of the roll cage mounting plate. Also the reverse light. Dimmable on MOSFET channel 7 (left) and 8 (right)
FLOOD_L.check: Light bars and pods dim with PWM? Test one on a cheap dimmer

HEAD_L.name: Left headlight (stock, 12 V 35/35 W)
HEAD_L.note: Dual filament bulb, low and high, one shared earth (Kawasaki 2013 Teryx 750 owner's manual: headlight 12 V 35/35 W x 2)
HEAD_L.check: Unplug a headlight and photo the plug. Which pin is low, high and earth?

TAIL_L.name: Left tail / brake light (stock, 12 V 8/27 W)
TAIL_L.note: Dual filament bulb, 8 W tail and 27 W brake, one shared earth (owner's manual: tail/brake light 12 V 8/27 W x 2)
TAIL_L.check: Photo the tail light plug. Which wire is tail, brake and earth?

TAIL_R.name: Right tail / brake light (stock, 12 V 8/27 W)

LIMP_SW.name: Backup lights toggle (hidden)
LIMP_SW.note: The Teryx has no headlight switch, so the dash and the Pico do everything. This hidden toggle is the backup if the control box dies: it feeds both low beams, both tails and the trailer tail at full through diodes. Leave it off normally. The Pico also turns low beams and tails on by itself if the dash goes quiet with the key on

BEACON.name: Roof beacon (amber + white LED, steady-on)
BEACON.note: Sam's amber + white LED beacon (bought 18 Nov). Each colour stays on steady and the Pico flashes them at 3 Hz (NZ Vehicle Lighting Rule 11.1(2): 2 to 4 Hz), amber and white taking turns. White only when stopped: on the road only red or amber may show to the rear. Fits Sam's existing hole on the roof
BEACON.check: Count the wires. Common earth + one wire per colour is what this plan expects. If each colour has its own earth it still works (join the earths). If it has a mode wire instead (one + feed, cycles colours on a pulse), tell the dash thread

BRK_WINCH.name: 250 A breaker
BRK_WINCH.note: Manual reset breaker, also the winch's kill switch: push it off to make the winch dead. No isolator contactor (Sam, 18 Nov), so the XBull remote and hand switches work whenever this is on

WINCH_SOL.name: XBull solenoid box
WINCH_SOL.note: The remote socket's in and out lines are cut from the coils inside the box and rejoined through their own diodes (WN21, WN22), like the hand switches. Then the in.winch_remote tap sees only the remote, not the Pico's own relays 4-5 driving the coils (found by the system sim, 23 Nov: tapped at the coil, the Pico would stop its own winch pull)
WINCH_SOL.check: Photo the XBull solenoid box terminals and the remote plug pins

ACT_DIFF.name: Front diff lock actuator (50 mm, pot)

ACT_4WD.name: 2WD/4WD actuator
ACT_4WD.note: 50 mm actuator, or drive the stock Kawasaki electric 4WD actuator instead
ACT_4WD.check: Is the stock electric 4WD actuator still on the front diff, and is the dash 2WD/4WD switch still wired to it? Photo its plug

BRAKE_SW.name: Brake light switch (stock)
BRAKE_SW.note: Also feeds both brake filaments and the trailer stop pin through diodes, so the brake lights work at full even with the control box off
BRAKE_SW.check: Find the brake light switch's two wires and meter them. Feed one from the 6-way (way 6), the other is OUT. If the stock loom still feeds the switch, cut that feed so it's only on our fuse. The switch now carries both brake filaments plus the trailer stop lamps (about 8 A with bulbs): if its contacts look small, put a 12 V automotive relay after it

PARK_SW.name: Parking brake switch (stock)
PARK_SW.note: Foot pedal park brake, cable only, no actuator. This switch only senses it: it lights the red park brake light in the meter and tells the control box (in.park), which then blocks drive through relay 6 (docs/park-brake.md)
PARK_SW.check: Find the parking brake switch wire at the meter plug. Does it switch ground or 12 V?

EPS_ECU.name: Toyota Aqua EPS ECU (89650-52B51)
EPS_ECU.note: Owned with its power plug (B+, GND). Still need the signal plug (IG, CANH, CANL). Pin numbers TBC: Toyota's RAV4 EPS ECU has IG, CANH, CANL on one plug and PIG, PGND on the other
EPS_ECU.check: Photo both EPS ECU sockets (pin numbers) and the power plug's wire colours

EPS_COL.name: Aqua steering column (motor + torque sensor)
EPS_COL.note: Motor and torque sensor plugs go to the ECU on Toyota's own loom. For RC, the two torque sensor signal wires (TRQ1, TRQ2) are cut and go through the RC changeover relay; the sensor's own 5 V and ground stay as Toyota wired them
EPS_COL.check: Measure the space from the steering wheel to where the Teryx shaft goes to the rack. Meter TRQ1/TRQ2 at centre, hard left and hard right effort (Toyota: about 2.5 V centre, the two moving in opposite directions)

RC_PICO.name: RC box Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (spare from the 5-pack)
RC_PICO.note: Second Pico, only for RC. Drives the steering by faking the torque sensor. If it stops or loses power the changeover relay drops and the real torque sensor is back. Pins TBC in the RC firmware; these are a starting point

RC_CAN.name: MCP2515 CAN module (RC box, main bus)
RC_CAN.note: Same 3.3 V-converted board as the control box (TJA1050 swapped for SN65HVD230). A short stub off the main bus inside the control box, no terminator

RC_LVL.name: I2C level shifter, 4-ch BSS138 (3.3 V to 5 V)
RC_LVL.note: The DAC and ADC run on 5 V so they can reach the torque sensor's range (up to about 3.5 V). The Pico's I2C is 3.3 V, so it goes through this

RC_DAC.name: MCP4728 4-ch 12-bit DAC (0x60)
RC_DAC.note: VOUTA = fake TRQ1, VOUTB = fake TRQ2 (a mirrored pair about the centre, trq_volts() in teryx/rc_mode.py). C and D spare (throttle wiper later). VDD 5 V, so 0-5 V out

RC_ADC.name: ADS1115 ADC (third one, 0x48 on the RC box's own I2C)
RC_ADC.note: Reads back what actually reaches the ECU (A0 TRQ1, A1 TRQ2) and the steering angle (A2). If TRQ1/TRQ2 stop mirroring, the RC box drops the relay. VDD 5 V so it can read up to 5 V

RC_REL.name: DPDT signal relay module, 5 V coil, gold contacts
RC_REL.note: Off (NC) = the real torque sensor goes to the ECU. On (NO) = the DAC does. Not the 16-ch board: its 10 A silver contacts aren't made for tiny sensor currents. The coil only gets power from the RC box, so anything that stops the RC box hands the steering back

RC_ANGLE.name: AS5600 magnetic angle sensor + magnet
RC_ANGLE.note: Steering angle for the RC steering loop. The bought Aqua column has no clock spring or angle sensor, so the AS5600 sits on a small printed gear driven off the column, geared down so lock to lock is under one turn, magnet on that gear. Analogue OUT (not I2C) because it's a long run from the cab. May not be needed if the Aqua ECU sends the angle on 0x260 (bench test step 4, docs/power-steering-aqua.md)
RC_ANGLE.check: Fit check: magnet centred over the chip, 1-2 mm gap (spec 0.5-3 mm), gear backlash small enough to hold centre

TRAILER.name: 7-pin flat trailer socket (Narva 82043BL, reed switch)
TRAILER.check: Which way does the Narva reed switch switch, and what triggers it?

TCAM_PLUG.name: Trailer EU 7-pin round plug (camera + light bar, Sam's)
TCAM_PLUG.note: Sam's EU round 7-pin, next to the flat NZ/AU 7-pin for the main trailer lights, so they can't be mixed up. NOT wired to the EU light standard. 1 cam +12 V, 2 video, 3 cam ground, 4 video shield, 5 light bar +12 V, 6 light bar - (switched), 7 spare. Light bar on 1.5 mm² (pins are good for 10 A+). Spring cap on the socket and dielectric grease on the pins

CAM_TRAILER.name: Trailer camera (12 V car camera, CVBS/PAL mode)

TCAM_DONGLE.name: Analogue video to camera-ribbon (CSI) board, ADV728x-M (front + rear + trailer, cabin later)
TCAM_DONGLE.note: No USB (Sam). ALL the cameras are car cameras in CVBS (PAL) mode into this one board, which sits in the Pi box on the Pi's camera ribbon port (CSI1). The Pi Camera Module 3 is dropped (26 Nov, PB Tech had none and Sam has car cameras). Inputs picked in software (adv728x-m overlay, adv7180 driver): input 0 rear, 1 trailer, 2 cabin (later), 3 front. The chip has 6-8 inputs (ADV7280-M 8, ADV7281-M/ADV7282-M 6) but cheap boards only bring some out to plugs: needs 3 now, 4 with the cabin camera. ONE decoder: only one camera is live at a time, the others show their last picture (or take turns, see docs/cameras.md). Pi 5 support for these boards is not proven yet: bench test it first
TCAM_DONGLE.check: Count the video inputs on the board (need 3, 4 with the cabin cam). Confirm it works on the Pi 5 (dtoverlay=adv728x-m,adv7280m=1); set each camera to CVBS/PAL, not AHD (OSD menu, button or mode wire)

PI5.name: Raspberry Pi 5 8GB
PI5.note: The 40-pin header and the PCIe port are kept for the AI HAT+ 2. CAN module wires go to header pins that come up through the HAT

CSI0.desc: free (no Pi camera now; all cameras on the video board)

HAT_HDR.desc: 40-pin header to the 16 mm stacking header

AIHAT.name: AI HAT+ 2 (later)
AIHAT.note: Not buying yet. Room, cooling (about 4.5 W) and the PCIe port stay free for it

PI_CAN.name: MCP2515 CAN module (Pi)
PI_CAN.note: Blue MCP2515 board with the SN65HVD230 swap (as the control box one), on the Pi box wall. 8 MHz crystal: pi-setup.sh default

SCREEN.name: 10.1 in touch screen
SCREEN.note: 1280x800, HDMI + USB touch, 3.5 mm audio in

GLOVE_USB.name: Glove box USB-C charger (RC phone)
GLOVE_USB.note: 12 V to USB-C PD socket for the phone that lives in the glove box (docs/rc-beach-launch.md 4b). Fed from the accessory relay so it's off with the key off
GLOVE_USB.check: Pick a 12 V USB-C PD panel socket (waterproof cap, about 20-30 W)

CAM_REAR.name: Rear camera (200 degree, Sam's)
CAM_REAR.note: Sam thinks it's AHD. Set to CVBS/PAL mode, soldered shielded video lead to the analogue-to-ribbon board. Rear or trailer is picked in software when the trailer plug is in. 12 V from the accessory relay (relay 7) through its own 2 A inline fuse
CAM_REAR.check: Rear camera: AHD with a CVBS mode? Photo its plug and label

CAM_FRONT.name: Front camera (12 V car camera, Sam's best of the 3)
CAM_FRONT.note: Replaces the Pi Camera Module 3 (26 Nov). Use the best of Sam's 3 AliExpress car cameras here: the front is the dashcam and the trail view at speed, so detail matters most. CVBS/PAL mode, not AHD. Mount behind the grille or on the bull bar, looking ahead, not mirrored. 12 V from the accessory relay (relay 7) through its own 2 A inline fuse, shielded video lead to video board input 3
CAM_FRONT.check: Front camera: CVBS (PAL) or AHD with a CVBS mode? Photo its plug and label

MODEM_4G.name: SIMCom A7670SA 4G board
MODEM_4G.note: 6-pin header S G V K T R G. V takes 5-10 V: a soldered lead from the Pi buck (5 V). NEVER raw 12 V (10 V max, and the car runs 14.4 V with spikes). K is tied to ground on the board, so it starts by itself. T/R are 115200 baud TTL to the Pi's GPIO 15/14; measure T before connecting (3.3 V ok, else BSS138). Micro USB also on board. Its GNSS (FASE version, u.FL GPS socket on Sam's board) is the dash GPS too, so there is no separate USB GPS. Check on arrival that it gets a fix with the SIM out / 4G off. No USB: it's on the header pins (soldered leads), so texts, GPS and slow data only, no live video over 4G

DAC_HAT.name: PCM5102 I2S DAC board (on jumper leads)
DAC_HAT.note: Swapped 26 Nov from the official Raspberry Pi DAC+ HAT to a cheap PCM5102(A) I2S DAC board from AliExpress (Sam). The ID stays DAC_HAT so nothing else moves. Small board with a 3.5 mm stereo jack out, to the amp's RCA inputs with a 3.5 mm to 2x RCA lead and a ground loop isolator. Sits on standoffs in the right-hand end of the Pi box, off the Pi, so the top of the Pi stays free for the AI HAT+ 2. Joined by 5 male-to-female jumper leads (about 20 cm): GPIO 18 to BCK, 19 to LCK, 21 to DIN, 5 V to VIN, GND to GND. No I2C on this chip, so SDA/SCL stay free for the IMU. On the board: SCK tied to GND (most boards have a solder bridge for it, else a short jumper), FLT, DEMP, FMT low and XSMT high (unmuted), which is how the usual purple board comes. Overlay: scripts/audio-setup.sh --i2s hifiberry-dac. Nothing else on the Pi uses 18-21 (CAN is SPI0 + GPIO 25, 4G is UART GPIO 14/15). A dab of hot glue on the leads at both ends against vibration. Later the leads move onto the AI HAT's stacking header pins

AMP.name: 4-ch class D amp (AliExpress, 4 x 63 W RMS at 4 ohm)
AMP.note: Sam's pick. 4 x 63 W RMS at 4 ohm, or 2 x 200 W RMS bridged at 4 ohm; built-in 90 Hz high and low pass; 8-16 V; up to 33 A flat out (16.5 A on music); 145 x 100 x 45 mm. Channels 1 and 2 drive the Kenwoods (set the HPF on). Channels 3 and 4 bridged (200 W at 4 ohm) drive the Kicker KM104 sub (LPF on, gain set so it stays under the sub's 150 W RMS)

SPEAKERS.name: Kenwood KFC-2053MRB 8 in marine speakers (pair)
SPEAKERS.note: Sam has these. 8 in 2-way, 4 ohm, about 50 W RMS each (100 W the pair), 180 mm cut-out, about 86 mm mounting depth (Kenwood spec page). One amp channel each; speaker cable 1.5 mm² is plenty. In sealed printed pods on the roll cage (cad/parts/speaker_pod.scad, docs/speaker-pods.md); the cable goes in through a PG7 gland underneath each pod

SUB.name: Kicker KM104 10 in marine subwoofer
SUB.note: Sam has bought it (18 Nov). 10 in, 4 ohm, 150 W RMS, 30-500 Hz. On amp ch 3 + 4 bridged, low pass on (90 Hz, matches the pods' EQ handover). Sealed printed box under the seat, on hold until Sam scans the space. 1.5 mm² speaker cable
